description: Preview Markdown with an LLM translation side by side. Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code, your own Anthropic or OpenAI key, or a local model.
command.openPreviewToSide: Open Bilingual Preview to the Side
config.title: Markdown Translation Preview
config.provider: Translation provider. `vscode` uses a language model in VS Code, such as GitHub Copilot, and needs no API key. For Anthropic and OpenAI, store your API key with **Bilingual Markdown: Set API Key**; keys are kept in VS Code Secret Storage, never in settings.
config.provider.vscode: A language model in VS Code, such as GitHub Copilot: no API key
config.targetLanguage: Language to translate into, written as you would tell a translator, e.g. `Japanese`, `English`, `Simplified Chinese`. A document can ask for another language with `translate-to: French` in its front matter.
config.openai.baseUrl: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API, e.g. a company gateway, or a local server such as Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) or LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234/v1`). Leave empty for api.openai.com. Must be `https://` (or `http://localhost`). A server on this machine needs no API key. Only user settings can set this, so a workspace cannot redirect your key.
config.vscode.model: Language model for the `vscode` provider, as a model ID or family. Leave empty for the first GitHub Copilot model. **Bilingual Markdown: Choose VS Code Language Model** lists the models you can use.
config.reasoningEffort: How much the model reasons before it answers. `none` is the fastest and cheapest, and is usually enough for translation.
config.reasoningEffort.default: Send no reasoning parameter and use the model's default (for models that reject the parameter)
config.styleInstructions: Extra instructions for the translator, e.g. `Use the plain である style.`
config.glossary: Fixed translations for terms, as `{ "source term": "translation" }`. A workspace can also keep a glossary in `.vscode/translation-glossary.json`; these settings win for a term in both.
config.translateCodeComments: Also translate the comments in fenced code blocks, and show the code with its comments translated beside the original. Only the comment text is sent, never the code. The block's language must be named after the opening fence, as in ```` ```python ````; common languages such as JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C, shell, YAML, SQL and HTML are supported.
config.maxConcurrentRequests: Maximum number of translation requests in flight at once.
config.batchCharacterLimit: Approximate number of source characters sent in one request.
config.tokenLimit: Pause translation after this many tokens (input and output) in one VS Code session, and ask before going on. `0` means no limit. Counted only for providers that report usage: Anthropic, and OpenAI at api.openai.com.
config.syncScroll: Keep the editor and the preview scrolled to the same place.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: In Restricted Mode, the target language, style instructions, glossary, and code comment translation come only from your user settings: the workspace's settings, its glossary file and `translate-to` in front matter are not used.
